content:
Hello,

Today, AWS announced the general availability of AWS Clean Rooms Differential Privacy. I'm mentioning it because it is using a discrete Gaussian sampler that was implemented and verified in Lean using Mathlib. The development is open source and available on GitHub. The documentation of AWS Clean Rooms Differential Privacy mentions it.

I'm not sharing this news to advertise my work but because @Leonardo de Moura and @Scott Morrison suggested that it may be of interest to some of you. What is currently proved is that the discrete Gaussian sampler has the appropriate mass function. I had to deliver in a short amount of time while learning Lean4 and Mathlib4 so even though the proof is complete, it needs to be cleaned up and improved a lot.

Thanks Tristan for telling everyone here. As well as an impressive achievement by John, this is a great testament to Mathlib and formalized mathematics generally: this is some serious maths being used "in production"!
